input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: No audit right binding the Customer exists anywhere in the Agreement. Literal searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" each returned zero hits, and a full read of the document (a single section, p0000-p0074) confirms it: neither the Fees and Payment provision (p0023) nor the Use of Service covenants (p0025) creates any inspection, records-examination or usage-verification mechanic against us, and no provision grants Kubient direct or remote access to our systems. The only access language, in p0001, is operational cooperation so that Kubient can deliver the Services, not an audit or system-access right. Having no audit obligation at all is better for us than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access), so there is nothing to limit; proposing a redline would only invite an audit right the Vendor has not asked for. The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails only because there is no audit clause for the frequency pattern to match, which is not probative here.
